candidate_windows.window_text:
We jointly estimated the parameters of the cognitive model together with the hyperparameters and parameters of the neural linking model using multivariate tree-structured Parzen estimator random search (Bergstra et al., 2011) with Optuna (Akiba et al., 2019). For subjects $i = 1, \dots, N$ , sensors $s = 1, \dots, S$ , and held-out EEG time series data for subject $i$ at sensor $s$ $Y_{i,s}$ , we maximized the value $V$ : $$ V = \frac {1}{N} \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {N} \left(\max _ {s \in \{1, \dots , S \}} r \left(Y _ {i, s}, \hat {Y} _ {i, s}\right)\right) \tag {8} $$ which is the average across subjects of the maximal Pearson correlation of predicted and observed EEG response among all sensors. Table 4 shows the precise bounds for each parameter and hyperparameter in this search procedure. We evaluated 20 trials (random settings of parameters) for the baseline model (which only incorporated the L2 coefficient), and 500 trials for all other models. The model results presented in this paper (in visualizations and statistical tests) correspond to the highest-performing outcome of each grid search. Table 5 shows the total count of free parameters under optimization. These counts do not include the parameters of the language model used to compute word surprisal, or the word recognition model ![](images/f54a36f1bfc257746b694a5c81ad4487d3026dcdb40280018ba776a8bbdd684e.jpg) Figure 8: Modulation of scalp voltage at a centro-parietal site by surprisal for words of different recognition time quantiles (according to the variable model of Figure 3), estimated on EEG data band-pass filtered with a low-cut of $0.3\mathrm{Hz}$ . Table 4: Specifications for parameter and hyperparameter bounds in random search. For details on the meaning of these parameters, see Table 1.
(Hyper)ParameterBoundsNotes
Regression L2 coefficient[102, 107]Logarithmic space. Bounds manually selected and restricted based on early runs of each model in order to reduce total runtime
γ (recognition threshold)(0, 1)
λ (evidence temperature)[0.1, 3]
α (scatter point)[0, 1]
αp (prior scatter point)[0, 1]
likelihood parameters, since these were kept fixed during optimization. All temporal receptive field models were fit with a receptive field ranging from $0\mathrm{ms}$ to 750 ms post word onset. We implemented all training and inference with GPU operations in PyTorch. Due to the large memory requirements of the EEG time series data and the lagged regression computations, we deployed each model fit on two NVIDIA A100 GPUs. Each of the model fits completed in two days or fewer. Table 5: Number of free parameters in all fitted models.
